tasks.prompt: List the name and city of every customer.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT name, city FROM customers
hints: Choose the two columns after SELECT, then name the table after FROM.

tasks.prompt: Show each product's name and its price with 18% GST added, as a column called price_with_gst.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT name, price * 1.18 AS price_with_gst FROM products
hints: You can calculate inside SELECT: price * 1.18. Name it with AS.

tasks.prompt: Find the names of customers who live in Lucknow or Varanasi AND signed up after 2025-03-01.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE (city = 'Lucknow' OR city = 'Varanasi') AND signup_date > '2025-03-01'
hints: Mix of OR and AND: do you need brackets?

variants.query: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city = 'Lucknow' OR city = 'Varanasi' AND signup_date > '2025-03-01'
variants.note: AND is evaluated before OR, so the date test only applied to Varanasi.

tasks.prompt: List the names of products whose name contains the text 'Pen'.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%Pen%'
hints: LIKE needs wildcard characters to mean 'contains'.

variants.query: SELECT name FROM products WHERE name LIKE 'Pen'
variants.note: Without % the pattern must match the whole name.

tasks.prompt: Find the names of customers whose city is missing (NULL).
tasks.reference_query: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city IS NULL
hints: NULL is not a value you can compare with =

variants.query: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city = NULL
variants.note: `= NULL` is never true; use IS NULL.

tasks.prompt: List the ids of orders whose status is not 'delivered' — including orders that have no status recorded.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE status <> 'delivered' OR status IS NULL
hints: What does <> do with a NULL status?

variants.query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE status <> 'delivered'
variants.note: Rows with a NULL status are dropped by <>.

tasks.prompt: Show the names and prices of the 3 most expensive products.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 3
hints: Sort first, then limit.

variants.query: SELECT name, price FROM products LIMIT 3
variants.note: Without ORDER BY the 'first 3' rows are arbitrary, not the most expensive.

tasks.prompt: List each distinct city that has at least one customer (ignore customers with no city).
tasks.reference_query: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM customers WHERE city IS NOT NULL
hints: DISTINCT removes repeated values; also exclude NULL cities.

tasks.prompt: How many orders have a status recorded (status is not NULL)? Return a single number.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT COUNT(status) FROM orders
hints: COUNT(*) and COUNT(column) are not the same.

variants.note: COUNT(*) counts every row, including the order with no status.

tasks.prompt: What is the highest and the lowest order amount? Return two columns: max_amount and min_amount.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT MAX(amount) AS max_amount, MIN(amount) AS min_amount FROM orders
hints: MAX and MIN are aggregate functions.

tasks.prompt: Show each customer_id with the total amount of their orders (column named total).
tasks.reference_query: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id
hints: One result row per customer needs GROUP BY.

variants.query: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM orders
variants.note: Without GROUP BY the SUM collapses everything into a single row.

tasks.prompt: How many orders are there for each status? Include the group of orders with no status. Columns: status, n.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY status
hints: NULL values form their own group.

tasks.prompt: Show the customer_id and number of orders (column n) for customers who placed MORE THAN ONE order.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
hints: Which clause can filter on COUNT(*)?

variants.query: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE COUNT(*) > 1 GROUP BY customer_id
variants.note: WHERE runs before grouping, so it cannot see COUNT(*). Use HAVING.

tasks.prompt: List every order id together with the name of the customer who placed it.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT o.id, c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
hints: How do orders and customers relate? Which columns match?

variants.query: SELECT o.id, c.name FROM orders o, customers c
variants.note: No join condition: every order was paired with every customer (12 x 8 = 96 rows).

tasks.prompt: Show each product name with the total quantity sold (column total_qty), only for products that have been sold.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.qty) AS total_qty FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.name
hints: Join products to order_items, then group.

tasks.prompt: List ALL customers with the number of orders they placed (column n_orders). Customers with no orders must appear with 0.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS n_orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name
hints: Which table must keep all its rows? Which column should COUNT look at?

variants.query: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS n_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name
variants.note: An INNER JOIN drops customers with no orders.

variants.query: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS n_orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name
variants.note: COUNT(*) counts the NULL-padded row, so customers without orders show 1 instead of 0.

tasks.prompt: Find the names of customers who have NEVER placed an order.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL
hints: After a LEFT JOIN, unmatched customers have NULL in the order columns.

variants.query: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL
variants.note: An INNER JOIN never keeps unmatched customers.

variants.query: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id = NULL
variants.note: `= NULL` is never true; use IS NULL.

tasks.prompt: Show every customer name with the id of each of their DELIVERED orders (columns: name, order_id). Customers with no delivered order must still appear, with a NULL order_id.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT c.name, o.id FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'delivered'
hints: Where should the status condition go so unmatched customers survive?

variants.query: SELECT c.name, o.id FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
variants.note: A WHERE on the right table removes the NULL rows, turning the LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN.

tasks.prompt: List each distinct pair of customer name and product name that the customer has bought (columns: name, product).
tasks.reference_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.name, p.name AS product FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
hints: Chain the joins customers -> orders -> order_items -> products.

variants.query: SELECT c.name, p.name AS product FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
variants.note: Joining through order_items repeats pairs when a customer bought the same product more than once.

tasks.prompt: Show each customer name with the total of their orders' amounts (column total), using the orders table's amount column.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.name
hints: Do you need the order_items table at all for this question?

variants.query: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id GROUP BY c.name
variants.note: Joining order_items repeats each order's amount once per item, inflating the total.

tasks.prompt: List the names of products priced above the average product price.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT name FROM products WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products)
hints: Compute the average in a subquery.

variants.query: SELECT name FROM products WHERE price > AVG(price)
variants.note: An aggregate cannot be used directly in WHERE; compute it in a subquery.

tasks.prompt: For every order show its id and a label (column size): 'big' if the amount is 500 or more, otherwise 'small'.
tasks.reference_query: SELECT id, CASE WHEN amount >= 500 THEN 'big' ELSE 'small' END AS size FROM orders
hints: CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END
